name: Sweden
headline: Sweden: +1.4% growth in 2025, 2.6% inflation, debt 35% of GDP
sections: Sweden is a $677 billion economy (2025), the world's 26th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.4% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $73K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 12.5% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 2.6% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 8.1% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 8.9% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 24.3% (2025).
Gross government debt is 35% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 41% in 2020. The general government balance is −1.3% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +6.7% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 104% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.6% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 31% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 84.1 years (2024). Population: 10.7 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
